title: PDO Drug Screening Data for Evaluating and Training AI Drug Response Prediction Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.15769v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Anti-cancer drug response prediction (DRP) is critically important for precision oncology and therapeutic development. Currently, most DRP models are developed using drug screening data from immortalized cancer cell lines, which can differ substantially from patient tumors at the genomic and molecular levels, even though patient tumor response is the ultimate prediction target. To help bridge this gap and bring DRP models closer to their intended clinical application, we conducted four drug screening studies using patient-derived organoids (PDOs), which more faithfully recapitulate patient tumors than immortalized cell lines. These studies generated data for improving and evaluating DRP models, including multi-omics profiles of PDO lines, drug feature data, and treatment response measurements. translated_title: 用于评估和训练AI药物反应预测模型的患者来源类器官药物筛选数据
translated_abstract: 抗癌药物反应预测（DRP）对精准肿瘤学和治疗开发至关重要。目前，大多数DRP模型是使用永生化癌细胞系的药物筛选数据开发的，这些细胞系在基因组和分子水平上可能与患者肿瘤存在显著差异，而患者肿瘤反应才是最终的预测目标。为了帮助弥合这一差距并使DRP模型更接近其预期的临床应用，我们使用患者来源的类器官进行了四项药物筛选研究，这些类器官比永生化细胞系更能忠实地再现患者肿瘤。这些研究产生了用于改进和评估DRP模型的数据，包括类器官细胞系的多组学图谱、药物特征数据和治疗反应测量结果。利用这些数据，我们在三种模型构建场景下对多个公开可用的DRP模型进行了重新训练和评估。
tldr: 该研究发布了四项患者来源类器官药物筛选所产生的多组学图谱、药物特征和治疗反应数据，用以弥合永生化细胞系与患者肿瘤之间的差距，从而更贴近临床实际地评估和训练AI药物反应预测模型。
en_tdlr: This study presents multi-omics, drug feature, and treatment response data from four patient-derived organoid drug screening studies, bridging the gap between immortalized cell lines and patient tumors to enable more clinically relevant evaluation and training of AI drug response prediction models.
